newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks end up on buying by speculators,funds.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks end up on buying by speculators,funds.

text.p: Revival of buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators pushed Delhi stocks higher after an early lull on Monday, brokers said.
The benchmark index closed 13.97 points higher at 897.79, after dropping to 882.02 in early trade.
Traders said Reliance Industries, whose shares went up sharply after its one-for-one bonus share issue announcement last Thursday, fell under selling pressure on profit-taking.
FIIs were aggressive buyers in ITC Ltd, forcing short sellers to cover their positions, they said.
"Selling was easily absorbed, which suggests the market's sentiment seems to be bullish," said Yogesh Sethi of brokers Vinayaka Investments.
Reliance ended 0.45 rupee down at 371.55 rupees. TISCO closed 5.55 rupees higher at 191.
ITC rose 24.75 rupees to 555 on steady buying by speculators and foreign funds, brokers said.
Hindustan Lever rose 49 rupees to 1,444 while Hero Honda rose 6.30 rupees to 503.90.
ACC rose on speculation and higher Bombay market trends by 24.85 rupees to 1,430.75, brokers said.
